business_problem: Astro needed faster and more consistent metadata generation across its web and mobile platforms, but manual tagging slowed content operations, limited scale, created classification inconsistencies, and reduced the quality of the personalization signals used across its OTT experience.
solution_summary: Astro partnered with TCS to turn metadata tagging into an agentic AI workflow instead of a manual media-operations task. TCS used TCS AI VX Studio as the orchestration layer, running on Amazon Bedrock with the NOVA multimodal model so autonomous AI agents could inspect web and app visuals, detect interface elements, and generate semantic metadata such as titles, genres, and categories. Product and content teams stay in the loop through a human-feedback process that corrects outputs and continuously improves prompt behavior as layouts and content formats change. The modular architecture processes assets in parallel for scale, then feeds the enriched metadata into Astro's downstream analytics and recommendation workflows, giving the broadcaster a repeatable way to tag thousands of assets while keeping the model adaptive to new UI patterns.

data_flow: Visual content from Astro's web and mobile platforms is processed by autonomous AI agents running through TCS AI VX Studio on Amazon Bedrock with the NOVA multimodal model. The agents detect UI elements and generate semantic metadata, product and content teams feed corrections back through the human-in-the-loop process, and the enriched tags flow into downstream analytics and recommendation systems.
business_outcome: Astro automated a labor-intensive metadata function, dramatically cut manual tagging work, improved consistency and throughput across content operations, and strengthened the personalization signals that support a smoother digital entertainment experience for viewers.
